tools.name: get_provider_status
tools.description: Live status for one tracked provider: overall state, non-operational services, and open incidents, read from the vendor's official status feed. Accepts a slug, provider name, or product name (e.g., "claude" resolves to Anthropic). Use this first for any "is X down?" question.

tools.name: check_my_stack
tools.description: One verdict across up to 12 providers: whether any vendor in the list is reporting a problem right now. Use before debugging an integration failure to answer "is it us or them?" in a single call. Returns a shareable status-board link.

tools.name: list_active_incidents
tools.description: Every incident currently open across all tracked providers, most severe first. Optionally filter by severity (critical, major, minor, maintenance). Use to answer "what is down right now?" across the whole cloud landscape.

tools.name: get_incident_details
tools.description: Full detail for one incident: the provider's own update timeline in chronological order, affected services, severity, and resolution state. Pass the incident slug returned by list_active_incidents or get_provider_status. Use to read what the vendor has actually said about an outage.

tools.name: get_uptime
tools.description: Independent uptime record for one provider over a trailing window (7-90 days, default 30), computed from OutageDeck's own observations of the vendor's official feed: share of time free of major outages, strict uptime with partial outages counted as downtime, and total impaired durations.

tools.name: get_outage_report
tools.description: A reliability summary across every tracked provider over a trailing window (7-90 days, default 30): incident totals, severity and category breakdowns, the providers hit hardest by major outages, and the longest-running severe incidents. Use to answer "which vendors had outages recently?" or to compa

tools.name: search_providers
tools.description: Find tracked providers by name, product name, or fragment ("postgres", "auth", "claude"). Returns slugs to use with the other tools plus each match's current status. Use when a provider argument did not resolve or to discover what OutageDeck tracks.

tools.name: list_custom_providers
tools.description: Lists the custom providers on the caller's own OutageDeck account: vendors they registered themselves by pointing at a status feed we do not track in the public catalog. Requires an API key, and only ever returns that key owner's providers.

tools.name: add_custom_provider
tools.description: Registers a vendor OutageDeck does not track by pointing at its Statuspage or Instatus status page, so it joins the caller's account with live status, incident history, and alerting. Requires an API key and a plan that includes custom providers. The feed is read live before anything is saved, and it

tools.name: update_custom_provider
tools.description: Renames one of the caller's custom providers, points it at a different status page, or pauses and resumes its checks. Requires an API key. A new address is read live before it is stored.

tools.name: remove_custom_provider
tools.description: Deletes one of the caller's custom providers and its stored incident history, freeing a slot on their plan. Requires an API key.

tools.name: watch_provider
tools.description: Starts sending the caller outage alerts for one provider, either from the tracked catalog or from their own custom providers. Requires an API key. Alerts are emailed to the account address; the other channels (Slack, Teams, Discord, webhook) are set up on the account page, so no webhook URL ever has

tools.name: search
tools.description: Search everything OutageDeck tracks: cloud and SaaS providers, and their incident history. Returns citable results with stable ids for the fetch tool. Use for open questions like "who had outages last week" or "find the GitHub Actions incident"; use get_provider_status when the question is simply wh

tools.name: fetch
tools.description: Retrieve the full text of one search result by its id: a provider's current status with its services and open incidents, or an incident's complete timeline. Ids come from the search tool.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "add_custom_provider" references sensitive artifacts (credentials). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "fetch" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_provider_status, get_uptime, list_custom_providers, add_custom_provider · Private data: get_uptime, list_custom_providers, add_custom_provider, update_custom_provider, remove_custom_provider, watch_provider · Public sink: get_uptime, watch_provider · Destructive: remove_custom_provider.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_provider_status, get_uptime, list_custom_providers, add_custom_provider · Private data: get_uptime, list_custom_providers, add_custom_provider, update_custom_provider, remove_custom_provider, watch_provider · Public sink: get_uptime, watch_provider · Destructive: remove_custom_provider

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
